title: A new commandment (John 13:31–38)
hookLine: love one another as I have loved you; by this all will know

cards: Why is the Thursday before Easter called Maundy Thursday? Maundy is an odd word; outside this one week, English hardly uses it. It comes from Latin.
In the old Latin Bible, today's verse begins with the words mandatum novum, a new commandment. Mandatum became maundy.
So a whole day of the Christian year is named after one sentence Jesus spoke at supper, right after Judas walked out into the night. The room is quieter now.
And Jesus speaks to the eleven who are left, like a father at the end.

teach.b: He calls them little children, the only time in John's Gospel he does, and tells them he's going where they can't follow yet.
Then: "A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another." Love one another isn't new on its own.
The law of Moses already says, love thy neighbor as thyself, and Jesus himself quoted it.
So what's new? The measure: not as you love yourself, but as I have loved you. They've just seen it: a towel, a basin, and feet, including the feet of the one who left.
Then the sign: "By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another." Not by a badge, a building, or a set of correct opinions. By love they can see.

teach.h: SEE HOW THEY LOVE ONE ANOTHER.
teach.b: Around the year two hundred, a Christian writer in North Africa named Tertullian reported what outsiders said of the Christians they knew: see how they love one another. Then Peter interrupts: why can't I follow you now?

teach.h: PETER: I WILL LAY DOWN MY LIFE.
teach.b: "I will lay down my life for thy sake." He means it.

And Jesus answers with sad honesty: "The cock shall not crow, till thou hast denied me thrice." Even the friend who promises the most will fail tonight. The new commandment is given to people who will need it.
Look back over this week: a frightened council, nard filling a house, a grain of wheat, walking in the light, a towel and basin, a disciple leaning close, and now love as the sign.

how: Christians remember the new commandment on Maundy Thursday, often with footwashing, communion and the stripping of the altar; many churches also take it as the measure of their common life.

p: see how they love one another

s: love your neighbor was first commanded by Jesus
it's in the law of Moses, Leviticus 19:18. the new part is "as I have loved you."
Maundy comes from the Latin word for commandment
Peter promised to lay down his life for Jesus
and Jesus told him he'd deny him three times before the rooster crowed.

games.q: you're Peter. Jesus says he's going where you can't follow yet. what do you say?
o: "I will lay down my life for thy sake."
games.why: Peter means it. Jesus answers: "the cock shall not crow, till thou hast denied me thrice."

practice: Think of someone whose love for you has been visible, not just felt but seen, and what they did.

Then think of someone you love, maybe not visibly enough, and picture one thing they would actually see: a note, a meal, an hour, showing up. If you pray, ask to love as you've been loved; if not, simply decide on the one thing.

orig.note: Greek: new, fresh. A new commandment: the old command to love, with a new measure.
